The '''Veronese map''' of degree 2 is a mapping from <math>\R^{n+1}</math> to the space of [[symmetric matrices]] <math>(n+1){\times}(n+1)</math> defined by the formula:<ref>{{cite book |title=Lectures on Discrete Geometry |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-0-387-95374-8 |page=244 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0N5RVe5lKQUC&pg=PA244 |language=en}}</ref>
:<math>V\colon(x_0,\dots,x_n)\to
\begin{pmatrix}
x_0\cdot x_0&x_0\cdot x_1&\dots&x_0\cdot x_n
\\
x_1\cdot x_0&x_1\cdot x_1&\dots&x_1\cdot x_n
\\
\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots
\\
x_n\cdot x_0&x_n\cdot x_1&\dots&x_n\cdot x_n
\end{pmatrix}.</math>
Note that <math>V(x)=V(-x)</math> for any <math>x\in\R^{n+1}</math>.

In particular, the restriction of <math>V</math> to the unit sphere <math>\mathbb{S}^n</math> factors through the [[projective space]] <math>\R\mathrm{P}^n</math>, which defines the '''Veronese embedding''' of <math>\R\mathrm{P}^n</math>. The image of the Veronese embedding is called the '''Veronese submanifold''', and for <math>n=2</math> it is known as the [[Veronese surface]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hazewinkel |first1=Michiel |author-link=Michiel Hazewinkel |title=Encyclopaedia of Mathematics: Stochastic Approximation — Zygmund Class of Functions |date=31 January 1993 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-1-55608-008-1 |page=416 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1ttmCRCerVUC&pg=PA416 |language=en}}</ref>

==Properties==
*The matrices in the image of the Veronese embedding correspond to projections onto one-dimensional subspaces in <math>\R^{n+1}</math>. They can be described by the equations:
*:<math>A^T=A,\quad \mathrm{tr}\,A=1,\quad A^2=A.</math>
:In other words, the matrices in the image of <math>\R\mathrm{P}^n</math> have unit [[matrix trace|trace]] and unit norm. Specifically, the following is true:
:*The image lies in an [[affine space]] of dimension <math>n+\tfrac {n\cdot(n+1)}2</math>.
:*The image lies on an <math>(n-1+\tfrac {n\cdot(n+1)}2)</math>-sphere with radius <math>r_n= \sqrt{1-\tfrac1{n+1}}</math>.
:**Moreover, the image forms a [[Minimal surface|minimal submanifold]] in this sphere.
*The Veronese embedding induces a [[Riemannian metric]] <math>2\cdot g</math>, where <math>g</math> denotes the canonical metric on <math>\R\mathrm{P}^{n-1}</math>.
*The Veronese embedding maps each geodesic in <math>\R\mathrm{P}^{n-1}</math> to a circle with radius <math>\tfrac1{\sqrt{2}}</math>.
**In particular, all the [[normal curvature]]s of the image are equal to <math>\sqrt{2}</math>.
*The Veronese manifold is '''extrinsically symmetric''', meaning that reflection in any of its normal spaces maps the manifold onto itself.

==Variations and generalizations==
Analogous Veronese embeddings are constructed for complex and quaternionic projective spaces, as well as for the [[Cayley plane]].
